title: Perfusion of Human Axillary Lymph Nodes for Real-Time Structure and Function Study
author: Llewellyn, Barrow-McGee, et al.

steps.title: Prepare Krebs‑Henseleit solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve all powders except calcium chloride in 990 mL double‑distilled water, stir ~5 min, add calcium chloride dihydrate diluted in 10 mL ddH₂O slowly, then filter through a 0.22 µm sterile bottle‑top filter inside a tissue‑culture hood.

substeps.instruction: Mix all powders (except CaCl₂) in 990 mL ddH₂O and stir for ~5 min.
Add CaCl₂·2H₂O diluted in 10 mL ddH₂O slowly to the mixture.
Filter the solution using a 0.22 µm sterile bottle‑top filter in a tissue‑culture hood.

steps.title: Set up thermoregulatory circuit
steps.instruction: Assemble the water‑jacketed circuit, pump distilled water through the glassware until it reaches 37 °C, and secure all connections to prevent leaks.

substeps.instruction: Connect the thermostatic water‑bath outlet to the glass reservoir inlet using 8 mm bore transparent PVC tubing.
Connect the reservoir outlet to the spiral heat‑exchanger inlet.
Connect the heat‑exchanger outlet to the petri‑dish warmer inlet.

Connect the petri‑dish warmer outlet back to the thermostatic water‑bath inlet; secure glassware on retort stands; tilt glassware after the bath is on to release trapped bubbles; ensure all connections are tightly screwed.

steps.title: Assemble perfusion circuit
steps.instruction: Connect the glass reservoir, peristaltic pump, heat exchanger, pressure transducer, and catheter using the specified tubing and stopcocks, and attach a half‑filled air damping syringe.

substeps.instruction: Load the Gilson Minipuls pump head with two tubing sets: purple 2.06 mm ID tubing to pump fluid into the cannulated ALN, and black 3.18 mm ID tubing to pump perfusate out of the petri dish (single‑pass) or back to the reservoir (recirculation). Ensure both tubes are taut and secured.
Connect the glass reservoir to the purple tube in the pump via a three‑way stopcock.
Split the pump outflow so that fluid passes through the spiral heat exchanger (to warm it) before entering the cannulated ALN, and simultaneously routes to the pressure transducer for feedback.
Attach a damping syringe (half‑filled with air) via a three‑way stopcock to the line feeding the pressure transducer to reduce pump‑induced pressure oscillations.
Position the pressure transducer at the same vertical level as the cannulated ALN artery.
Note: Steps 1–3 can be performed the day before the experiment if desired.

steps.title: Set up electrical feedback system
steps.instruction: Connect the PowerLab 26 series data acquisition system, Bridge Amp (single‑channel, non‑isolated) and STH Pump Controller according to the manufacturer’s schematic.

steps.title: Power on data acquisition system
steps.instruction: Switch on the PowerLab system before turning on the peristaltic pump to enable electronic pump control.

steps.title: Start peristaltic pump
steps.instruction: Turn on the Gilson Minipuls peristaltic pump and manually set the speed to 48 rpm using the pump buttons.

substeps.instruction: If the pump does not start, verify that the DIN cable is fully inserted at the back of the pump; if still unsuccessful, power off both the PowerLab and pump, then restart in the correct order.

steps.title: Fill glass reservoir
steps.instruction: Add filtered Krebs‑Henseleit solution to the glass reservoir.

steps.title: Prime perfusion circuit
steps.instruction: Remove all air bubbles by priming first the catheter line and then the pressure‑transducer line using the three‑way stopcocks and the STH Pump Controller.

substeps.instruction: Close the line leading to the pressure transducer.
Run the STH Pump Controller to push Krebs‑Henseleit solution through the catheter line until bubbles disappear.
Turn off the STH Pump Controller.
Close the catheter line and open the line to the pressure transducer.
Squeeze the pressure transducer tubing to allow fluid to flow through it, preferably into a collection beaker.
Run the STH Pump Controller again to prime the pressure‑transducer line until bubbles disappear.
Turn off the STH Pump Controller and stop squeezing the pressure transducer.
Reset all three‑way stopcocks to permit flow in both directions.

steps.title: Calibrate pressure channel
steps.instruction: Use LabChart’s two‑point calibration function to calibrate pressure readings in the pressure channel.

steps.title: Calibrate flow channel
steps.instruction: Use LabChart’s two‑point calibration function to calibrate flow readings; for reproducibility, select a fixed pump speed (e.g., 17 rpm) and calibrate at that speed for all experiments.

steps.title: Deliver Carbogen gas
steps.instruction: Connect a 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ gas canister to the circuit, turn on the gas at least 15 min before node insertion, and bubble the gas into the reservoir using a gas distribution stick.

substeps.instruction: Attach a two‑stage adjustable medical‑gas bull‑nose regulator with a Schrader valve to the gas canister.
Connect a gas flow meter to the Schrader valve.
Link the gas flow meter to the glass gas‑distribution stick using 5 mm bore silicone tubing.
Open the gas supply on the canister with a gas key and spanner.
Open the dial on the two‑stage regulator; the dials should rise sequentially indicating gas flow.
Lower the gas‑distribution stick into the fluid in the glass reservoir to act as a bubble oxygenator.
Adjust the gas flow meter to maintain a gentle, steady stream of bubbles, using the visual bubble level as a guide.

steps.title: Check pH with iStat
steps.instruction: After the fluid has been gassed for at least 15 min, take an iStat measurement and confirm that the pH is 7.4.

steps.title: Remove priming catheter
steps.instruction: Discard the catheter used for priming and leave the final three‑way stopcock open and ready to receive the cannulated ALN.
